customer_updates.text:
This was my second visit to Shalimar Restaurant. Last year I had visited during Ramzan for iftar, and this time I came for lunch. Honestly speaking, it feels more like a place known for its name and ambience rather than the food taste. The ambience is good and gives a premium feel, but the pricing is quite high for what you get.
We ordered cheese tandoori chicken and mutton biryani, and personally, I didn’t find the taste that great or worth the price. The total bill came to ₹1,575, which felt expensive compared to the overall experience. Also, the food service was delayed, even though it wasn’t extremely crowded.
Overall, it may be worth visiting once for the experience and ambience, but in terms of taste and value for money, it didn’t meet my expectations.

Had lunch at Shalimar Hotel in Byculla and decided to try their Bheja Masala with Butter Naan. Dining alone sometimes helps you focus on the food instead of conversations, which in this case turned out to be a good thing.

The Bheja Masala was exceptionally well prepared, fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. It had a rich texture and balanced spices that paired wonderfully with the soft, buttery naan. Every bite felt satisfying without being overly heavy.

The ambience is pleasant and comfortable, making it a nice place to enjoy a relaxed meal. The restaurant is well known for its Mughlai cuisine and offers a wide variety of dishes for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians.

Whether you're visiting with family, friends, or simply looking for a good meal on your own, Shalimar Hotel is definitely worth a visit. Great food, good ambience, and a consistently enjoyable dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

Your feedback on the food is invaluable, and we appreciate your thoughts on the dishes you tried. It’s great to know you enjoyed the Chicken Biryani!

We understand that expectations can sometimes lead to mixed experiences, and we'll take your comments about the flavors and service into consideration. Your insights help us improve and continually strive for excellence. We hope to welcome you back again in the future for an even better experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Sarvi: A No-Frills Culinary Gem in Nagpada
Nestled in the heart of Nagpada’s bustling chaos, Reza 'Sarvi' Cafe is a testament to the fact that real flavor doesn't need a neon sign. Housed in a weathered, historic building with nothing but a small, unassuming board to announce its presence, this place is a hidden gem sitting right in the midst of a busy road. If you are looking for "aesthetic vibes" or Instagrammable decor, keep walking—but if you are looking for pure, unadulterated soul food, you’ve arrived.
The Star of the Show: Mutton Seekh Kebabs
If there is one reason to brave the Mumbai traffic for Sarvi, it is the Mutton Seekh Kebabs. Hands down, these are some of the best kebabs you will ever encounter. They are melt-in-the-mouth tender, perfectly seasoned, and carry a legacy of spice that feels timeless.
The pairing with their Parathas is a match made in culinary heaven. Unlike the greasy versions found elsewhere, the parathas here are served hot, remarkably soft, and prepared with very little oil, allowing the richness of the meat to take center stage.
The Main Course & Appetizers
Aab Gosht Soup: A traditional start to the meal. While it was a decent, warming broth, it felt somewhat "okayish" compared to the high bar set by the starters. It's a subtle dish, perhaps overshadowed by the bolder flavors on the menu.
Mutton Masala Gravy: This is a "paisa vasool" delight. The gravy is thick, flavorful, and the meat is cooked to a point where it falls off the bone. It's the kind of hearty main course that reminds you why Sarvi has survived for decades.
The Sweet Finish
To end the meal, the Caramel Custard is an absolute must-order. It is easily the best caramel custard I’ve had in recent memory—silky smooth with the perfect balance of bitterness from the burnt sugar and the creamy sweetness of the flan. If you are a fan of 'Kharvas' you must try this.
The Vibe & Service
Sarvi doesn't pretend to be anything it’s not. The building is old, the furniture is functional, and the atmosphere is stripped back to focus entirely on the kitchen.
Service: Lightning-quick. The staff knows the drill and gets the food to your table while it’s still piping hot.
Price: Very easy on the pocket. You can eat like royalty here without a royal bill.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Timeless Kebab Haven

Hidden amidst the bustling lanes of Nagpada, Sarvi Restaurant is one of those rare gems that truly lives up to its legendary reputation. I had heard endless praises about their kebabs, but nothing could have prepared me for just how extraordinary they were. The first bite of their Seekh Kebab was enough to silence every conversation around me — tender, smoky, and meltingly soft, with a depth of flavour that only decades of mastery can produce. Honestly, they are the best kebabs I’ve ever eaten — a must-try for anyone who appreciates authentic Mughlai cuisine.

The place itself may not boast of fancy interiors or air-conditioned comfort, but that’s part of its charm. Sarvi’s old-world simplicity makes you focus entirely on what truly matters — the food. The aroma that greets you even before you enter is intoxicating, and watching skewers sizzling over charcoal is pure joy for any food lover.

Their Bheja Fry and Mutton Roll are also worth a mention, but it’s the kebabs that completely steal the show. If you’re a first-timer, skip the usual restaurant circuit and head straight to Sarvi. It’s not just a meal — it’s an experience that stays with you long after you’ve left.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mao Restaurant is a well-known dining spot in Mumbai Central, particularly noted for its extensive and varied menu. The restaurant boasts a wide range of cuisines, including Mughlai, North Indian, South Indian, Chinese, as well as fast food options like burgers and pizzas. I’ve also gone through and photographed their menu, which reflects just how broad their offerings are.

On this visit, I chose to mainly focus on Mughlai cuisine, which the restaurant is especially known for. The Dabba Gosht was excellent. It was rich, flavourful, and well-cooked, standing out as one of the highlights of the meal.

The Mutton Malwani was also very enjoyable, offering a good balance of spices and depth of flavour.

That said, Mao Restaurant is perhaps best known for its Kepsa Biryani, and I made sure to try both the chicken and mutton versions. Both were hearty, generously portioned, and quite satisfying. A filling and indulgent meal that clearly explains its popularity.

Service on this visit was slightly slow, though still acceptable. The ambiance is not really a highlight here. Even in the upstairs AC family section, the environment can get quite noisy. This is more of a place you visit for the food rather than for a quiet or relaxed dining experience.

Overall, if you’re in the Mumbai Central area and looking for a spot with strong Mughlai offerings and generous portions, Mao Restaurant is definitely worth trying, especially for its Kepsa biryani.

featured_reviews.name: Sharib k khan
featured_reviews.review_text:

The portion sizes are generally good for the price, and some dishes like biryani, kebabs, and gravies are quite satisfying when prepared well. However, consistency is the biggest issue - the taste and quality can vary depending on the branch and even the day you visit. Sometimes the food is fresh and flavorful, while at other times it may feel average or rushed. The ambience is simple and functional, not something you go to for aesthetics or comfort, but it works for a quick lunch or dinner. Service is also hit or miss; some staff members are helpful and fast, while others can seem inattentive or slow during busy hours. Cleanliness is acceptable but not impressive, so expectations should be kept realistic. Overall, Mao Family Restaurant is best suited for people who want reasonably priced food with decent quantity and familiar flavors, and who don't mind basic seating and inconsistent service. It's not a destination restaurant, but it does the job for everyday dining

Items are reasonably priced & the joint has a small in house eating area. Menu is different of Breakfast, Lunch, Snacks & Dinner. Must try once & you will love the food and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Onil Reginold
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this restaurant for dinner as a group of 10 family members. We ordered both starters and main course dishes.

The starters were served first, but before we had even finished half of them, the staff brought out the main course and started serving it as well. Even after we requested them to wait since we were still eating the starters, they placed all the dishes on our already crowded table and left. It became extremely inconvenient, as there was barely any space left even for our water glasses.

Another disappointing aspect was the service etiquette. The staff initially attempted to serve the main course on the same plates used for the starters. Only after we pointed it out did they replace them with proper dinner plates.

The biggest letdown was the food quality. The Murg Masalam we ordered was completely bland and tasteless. We had to add a lot of salt just to make it somewhat edible. Unfortunately, the experience got even worse the next morning, when 6 of us suffered from food poisoning, including loose motions and vomiting.

Overall, this was a very unpleasant experience, and I would not recommend this restaurant at all.
